title: North Hearing for the Proposed 2026 Solutions for Congested Corridors Program (SCCP) Guidelines
editorial_summary: The Commission agenda scheduled a northern hearing on the proposed 2026 Solutions for Congested Corridors Program guidelines for August 3, 2026. The Commission's August 20–21, 2026 meeting book items state that the North Hearing was held on that date. The Commission's meetings page now lists the hearing's presentation and a recording link beside the agenda. The presentation cites Order 5 and is recorded in the evidence register; the recording was not reviewed.
why_tracked: Directive 5 names the Solutions for Congested Corridors Program among the state funding programs whose guidelines are to be updated. The adoption book item that followed the hearing and the hearing presentation are in the evidence register; this lead now watches for a hearing record or adopted resolution text that documents the outcome.
evidence_boundary_note: The agenda, re-read on 2026-10-19, does not cite N-7-26, Executive Order N-7-26, or Order 5, and it does not record an adoption or hearing outcome. The hearing presentation that does cite Order 5 is a separate artifact with its own evidence record. The recording listed on the Commission's meetings page was not reviewed, so this note makes no statement about it.
relevance_rationales: n-7-26-5: The scheduled hearing concerns proposed guidelines for a funding program explicitly named in directive 5.
watch_for: A hearing record or the text of adopted Resolution G-26-60 that explicitly cites N-7-26. || Language showing whether the July 15 transit-priority and first- and last-mile proposals were retained in the adopted guidelines.
limitations: A scheduled hearing does not establish that any proposal was retained or that guidelines were adopted; the statement that the hearing occurred comes from a later staff memorandum, not from this agenda. || The hearing recording was listed on the Commission's meetings page but was not viewed or transcribed for this review.

title: FY 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity: Grants for Buses and Bus Facilities Infrastructure Programs
editorial_summary: FTA announced approximately $21 million for the FY 2026 Buses and Bus Facilities Program and approximately $589 million for the FY 2026 Low or No Emission Program. The page lists the opportunity as closed on September 21, 2026, the application deadline, and states that FTA will make selections within 75 days of that date. No selections were announced on the page at the October 19, 2026 review.
why_tracked: Directive 5 directs Caltrans to identify federal funding programs for transit-priority infrastructure and first- and last-mile projects. This new federal opportunity is a plausible program for later California guidance or identification, subject to project eligibility and scope.
evidence_boundary_note: The federal notice, re-read on 2026-10-19, does not cite N-7-26 and does not mention California, Caltrans or CalSTA. It is not a Caltrans or CalSTA identification action under directive 5.
relevance_rationales: n-7-26-5: The opportunity funds buses and supporting facilities and may become relevant to directive 5's federal-program-identification clause.
watch_for: Caltrans or CalSTA applicant guidance that identifies this program in connection with N-7-26. || A later California funding crosswalk or award record with an explicit directive citation.
limitations: The opportunity is nationwide, and not every eligible project is transit-priority infrastructure or a first- or last-mile project. || Topical relevance does not show that California will apply, identify the program under the order, or receive an award.

title: Caltrans Bay Area Completes First-of-its-Kind District Transit Plan with Release of Transit Needs Assessment Report and Map
related_urls: Caltrans District 4 Transit Plan: https://dot.ca.gov/caltrans-near-me/district-4/d4-programs/d4-transplanning-local-assistance/d4-office-of-transit-and-active-transportation/d4-caltrans-district-4-transit-plan || Transit Needs Assessment report: https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/district-4/documents/d4-office-transit-active-transportation-docs/d4-transit-plan/2026/tna-report-final-6-17-a11y.pdf
editorial_summary: Caltrans District 4 released a transit needs assessment and interactive map identifying Bay Area state-highway locations where bus-only lanes, safer crossings, and pedestrian or bicycle access improvements could support transit.
why_tracked: The district work is relevant to the statewide project-identification, design and permitting, and transit-priority assistance subjects in directives 1(a), 1(e), and 3(e). It may inform later statewide methods or materials even though it is not itself an N-7-26 deliverable.
evidence_boundary_note: The official release frames the plan and assessment as support for Caltrans Director's Policy 40; neither the release nor the reviewed report cites N-7-26. The assessment was finalized in December 2025 and is regional, not a statewide order deliverable.
relevance_rationales: n-7-26-1a: The assessment prioritizes state-highway locations for transit-supportive investment, which is relevant to the statewide priority-project-list subject. || n-7-26-1e: The associated district plan includes a toolbox for transit-priority and access infrastructure, adjacent to the design and permitting materials requested by directive 1(e). || n-7-26-3e: Bus-only lanes and transit access improvements overlap the technical-assistance subject in directive 3(e).
watch_for: A statewide Caltrans methodology, project list, or design package that cites N-7-26 and incorporates the district work. || A public crosswalk explaining how District 4 materials are used in the Section 1 deliverables.
limitations: Regional topic overlap does not establish statewide adoption, post-order causation, or delivery of any directive. || The plan and assessment describe planning resources, not evidence that technical assistance or a specific transit-priority project was delivered under N-7-26.
